+### Work a view started in itself: `netdiag.BackgroundMsg`
+
+`routeToView` is for work the router knows by name. A stop on the Ports tab
+(DEVDESK-711) is a chain of messages that a view sends to itself: the SIGTERM
+result, one probe per 250 ms tick, the SIGKILL result. They must reach netdiag
+whether or not `:net` is on screen, or the chain stops when the user leaves, `K`
+stays greyed and the row stays busy.
+
+The rule: a message type that belongs to such a chain implements
+`netdiag.BackgroundMsg` (an interface with one unexported method, so only
+netdiag's own types can). `App.update` has one case for it, before `default`, and
+`routeNetdiagWork` does the rest:
+
+| `:net` is | The message goes to |
+|---|---|
+| on screen | the active view, as any other message (`forwardToActiveView`) |
+| off screen | the netdiag view the router holds, through `routeToView`: `currentView` is untouched and the layout is not re-measured |
+| not open at all | nowhere: no view is created for it |
+
+Only netdiag's own types implement the interface
+(`TestOnlyNetdiagWorkIsBackgroundMessage` checks that a key, a resize, a ports
+read and an unrelated message do not), so no message the router already routes by
+another rule is redirected. A view that uses this road must also report
+`Running()` while the chain lives; netdiag does while a stop is pending, so
+naming it again from the command line does not rebuild it
+(`TestNamingNetdiagDoesNotDropAStopInFlight`). What the stop does is in
+`network.md`, « Two-step stop ».

## The footer's bar slot — `components.BarFrame`

`components.BarFrame(width, inner)` draws one line of already-styled content
inside the two-line rectangle that closes the viewport's bottom border, and
pads it to the width between the sides, so a caller measures nothing. It is the
only implementation of that frame (Rule 136). Its callers:

- `FilterBar.View()` — the table filter bar;
- the viewer's go-to-line prompt (`g`, `internal/ui/viewer/goto.go`);
- the workspaces fuzzy finder (`internal/ui/fuzzy/finder.go`).

Only one occupant uses the slot at a time on a given screen, and each appears
on demand. (The Path tab's target bar was the one that stayed in every state;
it went with the tab, DEVDESK-471, and the trace sub-level of Diagnostics has
no bar at all, a 3-line footer in every state.)

**The router reads the footer, not the view** (DEVDESK-457). `App.Render()`
renders the footer first; when `components.OpensWithBarFrame(footer)` holds
(ANSI-stripped line 1 framed by `│…│`, line 2 closed by `└…┘`), it turns the
viewport's bottom `└┘` into `├┤` so the two form one rectangle. Views no longer
declare a bar (`FilterBarVisible` is gone): whatever `RenderFooter` draws is
what the viewport joins. `fitHeight` trims a too-tall body just above its last
line, so that border survives a short terminal.

row busy. This also fixes a kill result lost the same way before DEVDESK-711.
  See `app-shell.md`, « Cross-View Communication ».

**Wording per platform (DEVDESK-710, DEVDESK-711).** Windows has no signal to
send: the process is ended at once through `TerminateProcess`, and the
confirmation promises nothing clean. `processOps.windows` selects the texts. The
key is `K` everywhere.

| | Linux, macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| `K` label in the header | `Stop process` | `Kill process` |
| Title | `Stop Process` | `Kill Process` |
| Body | `Ask <name> (PID <pid>) to stop?` + `Sends SIGTERM and waits up to 5 s. You can force it afterwards.` | `Terminate <name> (PID <pid>)?` + `Windows has no clean stop for this process: it is ended at once and cannot save anything.` |
| Row and footer | `Stopping <name> (<pid>)`, then `Waiting for <name> (<pid>) to exit` | `Killing <name> (<pid>)` |
| End | `<name> (<pid>) stopped` (it left within 5 s), `Process <pid> terminated` after a forced kill | `Process <pid> terminated` |
| Second confirmation | title `Force Kill`; `<name> (PID <pid>) did not exit within 5 s.` + `Force kill (SIGKILL)? It gets no chance to shut down cleanly.` | none |
| Help for `K` | `Ask the selected process to stop (SIGTERM), after confirmation; if it still runs 5 s later, offer SIGKILL (Ports tab)` | `End the selected process at once, after confirmation (Ports tab)` |
| `esc` | header `Stop waiting`, help `esc (Ports)` | none |

In the two Linux/macOS modals the process name is cut to 32 cells
(`stopNameWidth`), because `ConfirmModal` does not wrap and the lines must fit 80
columns. A name with no value reads `PID <pid>`. The Windows label stays free of
the word « Stop » (`TestWindowsLabelsPromiseNoCleanStop`): it must not suggest a
clean stop. A graceful close (`WM_CLOSE`) is a later story (S-04), not this one.

**Seams and the signal guard (DEVDESK-708, DEVDESK-709, DEVDESK-711).**
`internal/ports/procos.go` holds the seams the package reads about the host:
`selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos`, `now` (the listing instant and the Windows
budget) and `procOS` (an `osProcs` with `createTime`, `identity`, `probe(pid)`
and `kill(pid, want, sig)`; production value `realOS{}`). Per OS,
`identity_linux.go`, `identity_windows.go`, `identity_darwin.go` and
`identity_other.go` hold `readStatus` (`readIdentity` is its start stamp),
`heldIdentity` and `isNoSuchProcess`; `readStatus` returns
`errors.ErrUnsupported` on Windows and other platforms. In `netdiag`,

content.content:
| | Meaning | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| **UPPERCASE** | an action, global to the application | `TestNoViewBindsAnUndeclaredUppercaseKey` |
| lowercase | a filter or display toggle, local but **declared** per surface | `TestEveryLowercaseBindingIsDeclared` |
| `Ctrl` | only `ctrl+c`, `ctrl+r`, `ctrl+p` survive | `TestOnlyThreeCtrlCombinationsSurvive` |
| a modal's `y`/`n` | a *mode*, not a case — it takes every key before the view | declared in `modalKeys` |

`Shift` carries the actions because the other families are amputated: `Ctrl`
encodes only ASCII 0x40–0x5F and the tty confiscates four of them, `Alt` is not

**Out of scope.** `internal/ui/templates/form.go`, the rest of netdiag (the Path
tab's own field, Port and DNS Server), the `ctrl+p` palette and `FilterBar` do
not use the underline yet.

**Guards.** `internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go`:
`TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo` (Rule 119, `DefaultTheme` in `manager.go`
exempt), `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint` (no `Underline*`
outside `StyleInvalidField`), and `TestGuardDetectors` (the scanners fire on a
faulty fragment).
